code.method: SHA-256 over the sorted lines '<relative path> <file SHA-256>' of every file in the stratum package (D-077)

provenance.omitted: omitted from committed reports so that they regenerate byte for byte: a commit hash written into a committed file is always the parent of the commit that contains it. source_sha256 identifies the code (D-077).

declaration.description: SYNTHETIC FIXTURE REP-02: declaration states 3 runs per level; the data have 1 run per level with 6 wafers x 5 sites each (60 observations)

findings.message: 2 of 6 declared 'run' units have data. A whole run is missing, which v1 refuses rather than analyzing an unbalanced design. Designs outside v1 can be fitted in lme4 or lmerTest; Stratum does not analyze them.

explanation.text: Fewer experimental units (for example runs) have data than the declaration says, so at least one whole unit is missing. That unbalances the comparison, and why a unit is missing can itself matter. Stratum does not approximate around missing units; such data can be fitted with a tool for unbalanced designs, such as lme4 or lmerTest.

findings.message: 'temp' was applied to 'run' units, and level(s) {'low': 1, 'high': 1} have fewer than 2 of them in the data. With r < 2 there is no variation among units treated alike, so the test has no error degrees of freedom. More wafers or sites cannot replace replicated 'run' units.

explanation.text: The treatment was applied to whole units, such as runs, and at least one treatment level has fewer than two of those units in the data. Units treated alike are the only yardstick for judging a treatment difference, and with one per level that yardstick does not exist. Wafers and sites measured inside a run cannot stand in for more runs, because they all share that run's conditions. More units per treatment level are needed.
